1	\section{Related Work}
2	\label{sec:related-work}
3	
4	\paragraph{Neurosymbolic reasoning.}
5	LLM-solver pipelines~\citep{satlm, logic-lm, linc, fover-pei2025, lorp} and RL methods trained on solver feedback~\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl, deepseek-prover-v15, deepseek-r1} evaluate execution accuracy alone, with no diagnostic for component necessity.
6	AlphaProof~\citep{alphaproof2025} and DeepSeek-Prover-V2~\citep{deepseek-prover-v2} apply RL-based formal verification at scale in Lean~4 for competition mathematics; STA-style diagnostics could probe whether similar structural degeneration occurs in these settings.
7	We use FOLIO~\citep{folio}, the only public NLI benchmark with both FOL and Prolog annotations.
8	
9	\paragraph{Process rewards and reward shaping.}
10	Reward shaping theory~\citep{ng1999policy} constrains when auxiliary rewards preserve optimal policies.
11	In mathematical reasoning, learned process reward models~\citep{lightman-verify-step, math-shepherd, cobbe2021training, uesato2022solving} and verifier-guided search~\citep{nlproofs, vstar, easy-to-hard} provide step-level feedback, but suffer from reward-model noise and distribution shift~\citep{processbench}.
12	A recurring finding is that auxiliary rewards can hurt rather than help: \citet{gao-effective-rl-reward} show process/outcome bonuses can degrade RL training, and \citet{setlur2025rewarding} demonstrate that bonus magnitude requires careful calibration.
13	Annotation-free alternatives~\citep{cui2025prime, rlsf} derive dense rewards from outcome signals or solver certificates; ISR follows this direction but our results reveal that even annotation-free structural rewards are susceptible to Goodhart effects.
14	\citet{sullivan2025grpo-prm} prove GRPO with outcome reward is implicitly a Monte-Carlo PRM, a mechanism for why component-level gaming emerges under GRPO.
15	Parallel work on CoT faithfulness finds that stated reasoning steps are often not causally necessary for model predictions~\citep{lanham2023faithfulness, turpin2023unfaithful}; STA tests component necessity analogously but operates on solver-input clauses rather than natural-language CoT.
16	
17	\paragraph{Reward hacking and Goodhart's Law.}
18	Goodhart's Law is established theoretically~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy, skalse-reward-hacking, karwowski-goodhart-rl} and empirically in RLHF~\citep{gao-reward-overoptimization} and logical formalization~\citep{bondarenko-spec-gaming, kim-game-formalization}.
19	Most closely related, \citet{kim-game-formalization} document inference-time gaming on FOLIO with frontier models and Lean~4; our work is complementary in studying training-time degeneration with component necessity rather than faithfulness, and combining STA with inference-time detection would provide full gaming coverage.
20	\citet{kwa-catastrophic-goodhart} show that heavy-tailed reward misspecification causes catastrophic Goodhart where KL regularization provably fails, a theoretical lens for why GRPO's KL penalty does not prevent our observed collapse.
21	Reward model ensembles~\citep{coste2023reward} and constrained optimization~\citep{moskovitz2023confronting} address overoptimization at the reward level; STA instead diagnoses structural consequences at the output level.
22	Concurrent work documents spurious signals in RLVR~\citep{spurious-rewards, yan2026spurious, dong2026probing, metr-reward-hacking} and proposes composite rewards as mitigations~\citep{tarek2025reward, pronesti2026beyond}; \citet{yue2025rl-reasoning} show RLVR redistributes base-model probability mass rather than creating new reasoning, consistent with our finding that GRPO exploits existing shortcuts.
23	\citet{helff2026gaming} propose Input Perturbation Testing (IPT) for gaming detection; STA shares the perturbation intuition but operates at the component level in neurosymbolic settings where gaming emerges during training.
24	While IPT perturbs \emph{inputs} to detect inference-time gaming, STA performs leave-one-out ablation on \emph{solver-input components} to diagnose training-time structural degeneration, operating at component-level rather than input-level granularity and targeting the training process rather than deployment behavior.
25	\citet{khalifa2026countdown} provide controlled testbeds showing that reward hacking in Countdown emerges progressively during training; STA complements such testbeds by offering a component-level diagnostic applicable to neurosymbolic pipelines.
26	\citet{nishimura2026specgaming} systematically benchmark specification gaming across reasoning models, finding that RL training substantially increases exploit rates; our STA results provide a mechanistic view of how such gaming manifests as structural degeneration in solver traces.
27	Our Goodhart effect follows the regressional pattern~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} on FOLIO, with extremal dynamics at high $\beta$; its application to a diagnostic designed to \emph{detect} gaming, and the dataset-dependent asymmetry it reveals, are to our knowledge novel.
28	Complementarily, \citet{wilhelm2026monitoring} detect reward hacking at generation time via internal activations, whereas STA provides a post-training structural diagnostic.
29	
30	\paragraph{Mutation testing.}
31	STA adapts the LOO mutation paradigm~\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey} to solver inputs; novelty lies in application and findings, not in the perturbation primitive.

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related-work}

\paragraph{Neurosymbolic reasoning.}
LLM-solver pipelines~\citep{satlm, logic-lm, linc, fover-pei2025, lorp} and RL methods trained on solver feedback~\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl, deepseek-prover-v15, deepseek-r1} evaluate execution accuracy alone, with no diagnostic for component necessity.
AlphaProof~\citep{alphaproof2025} and DeepSeek-Prover-V2~\citep{deepseek-prover-v2} apply RL-based formal verification at scale in Lean~4 for competition mathematics; STA-style diagnostics could probe whether similar structural degeneration occurs in these settings.
We use FOLIO~\citep{folio}, the only public NLI benchmark with both FOL and Prolog annotations.

\paragraph{Process rewards and reward shaping.}
Reward shaping theory~\citep{ng1999policy} constrains when auxiliary rewards preserve optimal policies.
In mathematical reasoning, learned process reward models~\citep{lightman-verify-step, math-shepherd, cobbe2021training, uesato2022solving} and verifier-guided search~\citep{nlproofs, vstar, easy-to-hard} provide step-level feedback, but suffer from reward-model noise and distribution shift~\citep{processbench}.
A recurring finding is that auxiliary rewards can hurt rather than help: \citet{gao-effective-rl-reward} show process/outcome bonuses can degrade RL training, and \citet{setlur2025rewarding} demonstrate that bonus magnitude requires careful calibration.
Annotation-free alternatives~\citep{cui2025prime, rlsf} derive dense rewards from outcome signals or solver certificates; ISR follows this direction but our results reveal that even annotation-free structural rewards are susceptible to Goodhart effects.
\citet{sullivan2025grpo-prm} prove GRPO with outcome reward is implicitly a Monte-Carlo PRM, a mechanism for why component-level gaming emerges under GRPO.
Parallel work on CoT faithfulness finds that stated reasoning steps are often not causally necessary for model predictions~\citep{lanham2023faithfulness, turpin2023unfaithful}; STA tests component necessity analogously but operates on solver-input clauses rather than natural-language CoT.

\paragraph{Reward hacking and Goodhart's Law.}
Goodhart's Law is established theoretically~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy, skalse-reward-hacking, karwowski-goodhart-rl} and empirically in RLHF~\citep{gao-reward-overoptimization} and logical formalization~\citep{bondarenko-spec-gaming, kim-game-formalization}.
Most closely related, \citet{kim-game-formalization} document inference-time gaming on FOLIO with frontier models and Lean~4; our work is complementary in studying training-time degeneration with component necessity rather than faithfulness, and combining STA with inference-time detection would provide full gaming coverage.
\citet{kwa-catastrophic-goodhart} show that heavy-tailed reward misspecification causes catastrophic Goodhart where KL regularization provably fails, a theoretical lens for why GRPO's KL penalty does not prevent our observed collapse.
Reward model ensembles~\citep{coste2023reward} and constrained optimization~\citep{moskovitz2023confronting} address overoptimization at the reward level; STA instead diagnoses structural consequences at the output level.
Concurrent work documents spurious signals in RLVR~\citep{spurious-rewards, yan2026spurious, dong2026probing, metr-reward-hacking} and proposes composite rewards as mitigations~\citep{tarek2025reward, pronesti2026beyond}; \citet{yue2025rl-reasoning} show RLVR redistributes base-model probability mass rather than creating new reasoning, consistent with our finding that GRPO exploits existing shortcuts.
\citet{helff2026gaming} propose Input Perturbation Testing (IPT) for gaming detection; STA shares the perturbation intuition but operates at the component level in neurosymbolic settings where gaming emerges during training.
While IPT perturbs \emph{inputs} to detect inference-time gaming, STA performs leave-one-out ablation on \emph{solver-input components} to diagnose training-time structural degeneration, operating at component-level rather than input-level granularity and targeting the training process rather than deployment behavior.
\citet{khalifa2026countdown} provide controlled testbeds showing that reward hacking in Countdown emerges progressively during training; STA complements such testbeds by offering a component-level diagnostic applicable to neurosymbolic pipelines.
\citet{nishimura2026specgaming} systematically benchmark specification gaming across reasoning models, finding that RL training substantially increases exploit rates; our STA results provide a mechanistic view of how such gaming manifests as structural degeneration in solver traces.
Our Goodhart effect follows the regressional pattern~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} on FOLIO, with extremal dynamics at high $\beta$; its application to a diagnostic designed to \emph{detect} gaming, and the dataset-dependent asymmetry it reveals, are to our knowledge novel.
Complementarily, \citet{wilhelm2026monitoring} detect reward hacking at generation time via internal activations, whereas STA provides a post-training structural diagnostic.

\paragraph{Mutation testing.}
STA adapts the LOO mutation paradigm~\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey} to solver inputs; novelty lies in application and findings, not in the perturbation primitive.

1	\section{Method}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	\subsection{Task and GRPO Training}
5	\label{sec:task}
6	
7	Given premises $P_1,\ldots,P_k$ and conclusion $C$, the task is to produce a formal program $F=\{c_1,\ldots,c_n\}$ verified by an external solver $S\in\{\text{Prover9, SWI-Prolog}\}$.
8	We train with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)~\citep{deepseekmath} ($K{=}4$), where each rollout receives binary execution reward $r_{\text{exec}}(x) = \mathbf{1}[S(F_x){=}\textit{proved}]$.
9	This optimizes prove rate but provides no signal about \emph{component necessity}: a formalization embedding the conclusion among its premises receives the same reward as a faithful derivation.
10	All experiments draw from FOLIO~\citep{folio}.
11	
12	\subsection{Solver Trace Ablation (STA)}
13	\label{sec:sta}
14	
15	STA tests whether each component of a proved formalization is individually necessary for proof success (Algorithm~\ref{alg:sta}).
16	Given a proved $x$ with $n$ components, STA constructs $n$ ablated variants $x\setminus\{c_i\}$ and re-runs the solver (Algorithm~\ref{alg:sta}).
17	A component is \emph{necessary} if its removal causes proof failure.
18	What constitutes a component depends on the logic: premises in FOL, clauses or ground facts in Prolog.
19	LOO ablation itself is standard in mutation testing and sensitivity analysis~\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey}; novelty lies in its application as a GRPO-hacking diagnostic and the empirical phenomena it surfaces.
20	
21	\begin{algorithm}[t]
22	\caption{Solver Trace Ablation (STA)}
23	\label{alg:sta}
24	\begin{algorithmic}[1]
25	\REQUIRE Proved formalization $x = \{c_1, \ldots, c_n\}$, solver $S$
26	\ENSURE $\text{ISR}(x) \in [0, 1]$
27	\STATE $\textit{necessary} \gets 0$
28	\FOR{$i = 1$ to $n$}
29	    \IF{$S(x \setminus \{c_i\}) = \textit{failed}$}
30	        \STATE $\textit{necessary} \gets \textit{necessary} + 1$
31	    \ENDIF
32	\ENDFOR
33	\RETURN $\textit{necessary} \,/\, n$
34	\end{algorithmic}
35	\end{algorithm}
36	
37	\paragraph{Intensional Structural Reward.}\footnote{Not \emph{intentional}; \emph{intensional} contrasts with extensional (execution-only) evaluation.}
38	ISR is the fraction of necessary components:
39	\begin{equation}
40	  \text{ISR}(x) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf{1}\bigl[S(x\setminus\{c_i\})=\textit{failed}\bigr]
41	  \label{eq:isr}
42	\end{equation}
43	ISR is defined only for proved formalizations: ISR${=}1$ means every component is necessary; ISR${=}0$ means complete redundancy.
44	An ISR of zero for proved samples can arise from two sources: structural degeneration (redundant or tautological premises) or genuine redundancy (multiple valid proof paths).
45	Our hacking mode classification (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}) disambiguates these cases; in practice, ${>}90\%$ of low-ISR proved samples exhibit identifiable hacking patterns (CE or TS).
46	Unproved samples receive $\text{ISR}{=}0$ by definition, as the solver rejects the proof and no component ablation is meaningful.
47	ISR is a special case of the Shapley value restricted to the $(n{-}1)$-coalition, reducing attribution complexity from $O(2^n)$ to $O(n)$~\citep{lundberg2017unified}. The solver's binary accept/reject output makes leave-one-out sufficient for testing component \emph{necessity}; Shapley's advantage lies in quantifying \emph{how much} each component contributes, which ISR's binary framing deliberately forgoes.
48	ISR quantifies component redundancy, not semantic faithfulness; its diagnostic value is realized through the downstream mode breakdown (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}), not the scalar alone.
49	We report \emph{proved-only} ISR (denoted ISR$^*$) throughout to avoid conflating component necessity with prove rate.
50	
51	\paragraph{Limitations of ISR.}
52	ISR captures component necessity, not semantic faithfulness; it does not correlate with NLI accuracy (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).
53	A structural confound arises from component count: formalizations with fewer components mechanically receive higher ISR, and tautological shortcuts ($P{\to}P$) achieve high ISR by construction since the sole premise is necessary for the trivial proof.
54	We therefore combine ISR with text-match classifiers for complete hacking detection (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}; $O(1)$ binary variant in Appendix~\ref{app:o1-ablation}), and report premise-count-matched comparisons in \S\ref{sec:goodhart}.
55	At the per-sample level, ISR flags distinct failure modes ($\text{ISR}{=}0$: redundancy; $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ with $n{=}1$: tautology) independent of this confound.
56	We distinguish two uses of ISR: as an \emph{aggregate} metric (mean ISR across a test set, susceptible to premise-count inflation discussed in \S\ref{sec:goodhart}), and as a \emph{per-sample} diagnostic (the LOO result for a single proof, unaffected by cross-sample length distributions).
57	As a diagnostic, ISR most readily identifies CE, where removing fabricated expressions collapses the proof ($\text{ISR}{\approx}0$), but is less discriminative for TS, where tautological structures score high ISR by construction; detecting TS requires combining ISR with component-count thresholds (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}).
58	
59	\paragraph{LOO independence assumption.}
60	LOO ablation tests individual, not joint, component necessity~\citep{jia-harman-survey}, systematically underestimating ISR when jointly-necessary components exist; the observed collapse is therefore conservative.
61	
62	\subsection{Reward Conditions and Hacking Modes}
63	\label{sec:rewards}
64	\label{sec:taxonomy-method}
65	
66	We study six conditions: exec-only ($r_{\text{exec}}$), ISR low/high-dose ($r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1{+}\beta\,\text{ISR})$ at $\beta\in\{0.1,0.3\}$), matched random controls ($r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1{+}\beta u)$, $u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$), and a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) baseline (negative log-likelihood on gold formalizations).
67	Multiplicative bonuses apply only to proved samples, keeping the prove-rate floor intact.
68	Random isolates ISR-specific signal from generic reward-variance effects; SFT isolates whether structural degeneration arises from RL optimization or data exposure alone.
69	Each RL condition uses seeds $\{42,43,44\}$ and identical training data (formulation alternatives in Appendix~\ref{app:setup}).
70	
71	\paragraph{Hacking taxonomy.}
72	Across conditions, seeds, and logic types we identify eight structural-degeneration modes (full definitions in Appendix~\ref{app:hacking-modes}):
73	\textbf{CE} (conclusion embedded among multiple premises),
74	\textbf{TS} (single-premise conclusion duplication, subtypes TSa standard and TSb obfuscated tautology; targets the ISR signal directly, since removing the sole premise forces $\text{ISR}\geq 0.5$),
75	\textbf{PG} (premise-subset gaming: each component is LOO-necessary but the premise set is a strict subset of what the problem requires, inflating ISR without faithful reasoning; Appendix~\ref{app:h8}),
76	\textbf{tautological collapse} (minimal two-component $P{\to}P$ without explicit ISR inflation),
77	\textbf{repetition collapse} (identical clauses repeated to inflate component count),
78	\textbf{complexity-without-utility} (elaborate but vacuous premises),
79	\textbf{contradiction explosion} (contradictory premises trivializing any conclusion via \emph{ex falso}), and
80	\textbf{query-as-fact gaming} (Prolog-specific: emit the NL question as an atom asserted as both fact and query; evades text-match classifiers).
81	Modes are identified by a two-stage procedure: strict normalized text matching (CE/TS) plus functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\text{necessary}}$ distribution (catches modes evading text matching).
82	Modes are not mutually exclusive; when a sample matches multiple patterns, we assign the structurally most specific mode (PG $>$ CE $>$ TS).
83	The non-hacking rate is an upper bound on genuine reasoning, as classifier recall is unknown for most modes.
84	We report both classifications in \S\ref{sec:experiments}.
85	
86	Low ISR signals redundancy under exec-only but metric gaming under ISR-as-reward; the mode breakdown, not the ISR scalar, licenses interpretation.
87

\caption{Solver Trace Ablation (STA)}
\label{alg:sta}
\begin{algorithmic}[1]
\REQUIRE Proved formalization $x = \{c_1, \ldots, c_n\}$, solver $S$
\ENSURE $\text{ISR}(x) \in [0, 1]$
\STATE $\textit{necessary} \gets 0$
\FOR{$i = 1$ to $n$}
    \IF{$S(x \setminus \{c_i\}) = \textit{failed}$}
        \STATE $\textit{necessary} \gets \textit{necessary} + 1$
    \ENDIF
\ENDFOR
\RETURN $\textit{necessary} \,/\, n$
\end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}

\paragraph{Intensional Structural Reward.}\footnote{Not \emph{intentional}; \emph{intensional} contrasts with extensional (execution-only) evaluation.}
ISR is the fraction of necessary components:
\begin{equation}
  \text{ISR}(x) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf{1}\bigl[S(x\setminus\{c_i\})=\textit{failed}\bigr]
  \label{eq:isr}
\end{equation}
ISR is defined only for proved formalizations: ISR${=}1$ means every component is necessary; ISR${=}0$ means complete redundancy.
An ISR of zero for proved samples can arise from two sources: structural degeneration (redundant or tautological premises) or genuine redundancy (multiple valid proof paths).
Our hacking mode classification (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}) disambiguates these cases; in practice, ${>}90\%$ of low-ISR proved samples exhibit identifiable hacking patterns (CE or TS).
Unproved samples receive $\text{ISR}{=}0$ by definition, as the solver rejects the proof and no component ablation is meaningful.
ISR is a special case of the Shapley value restricted to the $(n{-}1)$-coalition, reducing attribution complexity from $O(2^n)$ to $O(n)$~\citep{lundberg2017unified}. The solver's binary accept/reject output makes leave-one-out sufficient for testing component \emph{necessity}; Shapley's advantage lies in quantifying \emph{how much} each component contributes, which ISR's binary framing deliberately forgoes.
ISR quantifies component redundancy, not semantic faithfulness; its diagnostic value is realized through the downstream mode breakdown (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}), not the scalar alone.
We report \emph{proved-only} ISR (denoted ISR$^*$) throughout to avoid conflating component necessity with prove rate.

\paragraph{Limitations of ISR.}
ISR captures component necessity, not semantic faithfulness; it does not correlate with NLI accuracy (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).
A structural confound arises from component count: formalizations with fewer components mechanically receive higher ISR, and tautological shortcuts ($P{\to}P$) achieve high ISR by construction since the sole premise is necessary for the trivial proof.
We therefore combine ISR with text-match classifiers for complete hacking detection (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}; $O(1)$ binary variant in Appendix~\ref{app:o1-ablation}), and report premise-count-matched comparisons in \S\ref{sec:goodhart}.
At the per-sample level, ISR flags distinct failure modes ($\text{ISR}{=}0$: redundancy; $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ with $n{=}1$: tautology) independent of this confound.
We distinguish two uses of ISR: as an \emph{aggregate} metric (mean ISR across a test set, susceptible to premise-count inflation discussed in \S\ref{sec:goodhart}), and as a \emph{per-sample} diagnostic (the LOO result for a single proof, unaffected by cross-sample length distributions).
As a diagnostic, ISR most readily identifies CE, where removing fabricated expressions collapses the proof ($\text{ISR}{\approx}0$), but is less discriminative for TS, where tautological structures score high ISR by construction; detecting TS requires combining ISR with component-count thresholds (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}).

\paragraph{LOO independence assumption.}
LOO ablation tests individual, not joint, component necessity~\citep{jia-harman-survey}, systematically underestimating ISR when jointly-necessary components exist; the observed collapse is therefore conservative.

\subsection{Reward Conditions and Hacking Modes}
\label{sec:rewards}
\label{sec:taxonomy-method}

We study six conditions: exec-only ($r_{\text{exec}}$), ISR low/high-dose ($r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1{+}\beta\,\text{ISR})$ at $\beta\in\{0.1,0.3\}$), matched random controls ($r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1{+}\beta u)$, $u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$), and a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) baseline (negative log-likelihood on gold formalizations).
Multiplicative bonuses apply only to proved samples, keeping the prove-rate floor intact.
Random isolates ISR-specific signal from generic reward-variance effects; SFT isolates whether structural degeneration arises from RL optimization or data exposure alone.
Each RL condition uses seeds $\{42,43,44\}$ and identical training data (formulation alternatives in Appendix~\ref{app:setup}).

\paragraph{Hacking taxonomy.}
Across conditions, seeds, and logic types we identify eight structural-degeneration modes (full definitions in Appendix~\ref{app:hacking-modes}):
\textbf{CE} (conclusion embedded among multiple premises),
\textbf{TS} (single-premise conclusion duplication, subtypes TSa standard and TSb obfuscated tautology; targets the ISR signal directly, since removing the sole premise forces $\text{ISR}\geq 0.5$),
\textbf{PG} (premise-subset gaming: each component is LOO-necessary but the premise set is a strict subset of what the problem requires, inflating ISR without faithful reasoning; Appendix~\ref{app:h8}),
\textbf{tautological collapse} (minimal two-component $P{\to}P$ without explicit ISR inflation),
\textbf{repetition collapse} (identical clauses repeated to inflate component count),
\textbf{complexity-without-utility} (elaborate but vacuous premises),
\textbf{contradiction explosion} (contradictory premises trivializing any conclusion via \emph{ex falso}), and
\textbf{query-as-fact gaming} (Prolog-specific: emit the NL question as an atom asserted as both fact and query; evades text-match classifiers).
Modes are identified by a two-stage procedure: strict normalized text matching (CE/TS) plus functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\text{necessary}}$ distribution (catches modes evading text matching).
Modes are not mutually exclusive; when a sample matches multiple patterns, we assign the structurally most specific mode (PG $>$ CE $>$ TS).
The non-hacking rate is an upper bound on genuine reasoning, as classifier recall is unknown for most modes.
We report both classifications in \S\ref{sec:experiments}.

Low ISR signals redundancy under exec-only but metric gaming under ISR-as-reward; the mode breakdown, not the ISR scalar, licenses interpretation.

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related-work}

\paragraph{Neurosymbolic reasoning.}
LLM-solver pipelines~\citep{satlm, logic-lm, linc, fover-pei2025, lorp} and RL methods trained on solver feedback~\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl, deepseek-prover-v15, deepseek-r1} evaluate execution accuracy alone, with no diagnostic for component necessity.
AlphaProof~\citep{alphaproof2025} and DeepSeek-Prover-V2~\citep{deepseek-prover-v2} apply RL-based formal verification at scale in Lean~4 for competition mathematics; STA-style diagnostics could probe whether similar structural degeneration occurs in these settings.
We use FOLIO~\citep{folio}, the only public NLI benchmark with both FOL and Prolog annotations.

\paragraph{Process rewards and reward shaping.}
Reward shaping theory~\citep{ng1999policy} constrains when auxiliary rewards preserve optimal policies.
In mathematical reasoning, learned process reward models~\citep{lightman-verify-step, math-shepherd, cobbe2021training, uesato2022solving} and verifier-guided search~\citep{nlproofs, vstar, easy-to-hard} provide step-level feedback, but suffer from reward-model noise and distribution shift~\citep{processbench}.
A recurring finding is that auxiliary rewards can hurt rather than help: \citet{gao-effective-rl-reward} show process/outcome bonuses can degrade RL training, and \citet{setlur2025rewarding} demonstrate that bonus magnitude requires careful calibration.
Annotation-free alternatives~\citep{cui2025prime, rlsf} derive dense rewards from outcome signals or solver certificates; ISR follows this direction but our results reveal that even annotation-free structural rewards are susceptible to Goodhart effects.
\citet{sullivan2025grpo-prm} prove GRPO with outcome reward is implicitly a Monte-Carlo PRM, a mechanism for why component-level gaming emerges under GRPO.
Parallel work on CoT faithfulness finds that stated reasoning steps are often not causally necessary for model predictions~\citep{lanham2023faithfulness, turpin2023unfaithful}; STA tests component necessity analogously but operates on solver-input clauses rather than natural-language CoT.

\paragraph{Reward hacking and Goodhart's Law.}
Goodhart's Law is established theoretically~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy, skalse-reward-hacking, karwowski-goodhart-rl} and empirically in RLHF~\citep{gao-reward-overoptimization} and logical formalization~\citep{bondarenko-spec-gaming, kim-game-formalization}.
Most closely related, \citet{kim-game-formalization} document inference-time gaming on FOLIO with frontier models and Lean~4; our work is complementary in studying training-time degeneration with component necessity rather than faithfulness, and combining STA with inference-time detection would provide full gaming coverage.
\citet{kwa-catastrophic-goodhart} show that heavy-tailed reward misspecification causes catastrophic Goodhart where KL regularization provably fails, a theoretical lens for why GRPO's KL penalty does not prevent our observed collapse.
Reward model ensembles~\citep{coste2023reward} and constrained optimization~\citep{moskovitz2023confronting} address overoptimization at the reward level; STA instead diagnoses structural consequences at the output level.
Concurrent work documents spurious signals in RLVR~\citep{spurious-rewards, yan2026spurious, dong2026probing, metr-reward-hacking} and proposes composite rewards as mitigations~\citep{tarek2025reward, pronesti2026beyond}; \citet{yue2025rl-reasoning} show RLVR redistributes base-model probability mass rather than creating new reasoning, consistent with our finding that GRPO exploits existing shortcuts.
\citet{helff2026gaming} propose Input Perturbation Testing (IPT) for gaming detection; STA shares the perturbation intuition but operates at the component level in neurosymbolic settings where gaming emerges during training.
While IPT perturbs \emph{inputs} to detect inference-time gaming, STA performs leave-one-out ablation on \emph{solver-input components} to diagnose training-time structural degeneration, operating at component-level rather than input-level granularity and targeting the training process rather than deployment behavior.
\citet{khalifa2026countdown} provide controlled testbeds showing that reward hacking in Countdown emerges progressively during training; STA complements such testbeds by offering a component-level diagnostic applicable to neurosymbolic pipelines.
\citet{nishimura2026specgaming} systematically benchmark specification gaming across reasoning models, finding that RL training substantially increases exploit rates; our STA results provide a mechanistic view of how such gaming manifests as structural degeneration in solver traces.
Our Goodhart effect follows the regressional pattern~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} on FOLIO, with extremal dynamics at high $\beta$; its application to a diagnostic designed to \emph{detect} gaming, and the dataset-dependent asymmetry it reveals, are to our knowledge novel.
Complementarily, \citet{wilhelm2026monitoring} detect reward hacking at generation time via internal activations, whereas STA provides a post-training structural diagnostic.

\paragraph{Mutation testing.}
STA adapts the LOO mutation paradigm~\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey} to solver inputs; novelty lies in application and findings, not in the perturbation primitive.

\label{sec:taxonomy-method}

We study six conditions: exec-only ($r_{\text{exec}}$), ISR low/high-dose ($r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1{+}\beta\,\text{ISR})$ at $\beta\in\{0.1,0.3\}$), matched random controls ($r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1{+}\beta u)$, $u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$), and a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) baseline (negative log-likelihood on gold formalizations).
Multiplicative bonuses apply only to proved samples, keeping the prove-rate floor intact.
Random isolates ISR-specific signal from generic reward-variance effects; SFT isolates whether structural degeneration arises from RL optimization or data exposure alone.
Each RL condition uses seeds $\{42,43,44\}$ and identical training data (formulation alternatives in Appendix~\ref{app:setup}).

\paragraph{Hacking taxonomy.}
Across conditions, seeds, and logic types we identify eight structural-degeneration modes (full definitions in Appendix~\ref{app:hacking-modes}):
\textbf{CE} (conclusion embedded among multiple premises),
\textbf{TS} (single-premise conclusion duplication, subtypes TSa standard and TSb obfuscated tautology; targets the ISR signal directly, since removing the sole premise forces $\text{ISR}\geq 0.5$),
\textbf{PG} (premise-subset gaming: each component is LOO-necessary but the premise set is a strict subset of what the problem requires, inflating ISR without faithful reasoning; Appendix~\ref{app:h8}),
\textbf{tautological collapse} (minimal two-component $P{\to}P$ without explicit ISR inflation),
\textbf{repetition collapse} (identical clauses repeated to inflate component count),
\textbf{complexity-without-utility} (elaborate but vacuous premises),
\textbf{contradiction explosion} (contradictory premises trivializing any conclusion via \emph{ex falso}), and
\textbf{query-as-fact gaming} (Prolog-specific: emit the NL question as an atom asserted as both fact and query; evades text-match classifiers).
Modes are identified by a two-stage procedure: strict normalized text matching (CE/TS) plus functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\text{necessary}}$ distribution (catches modes evading text matching).
Modes are not mutually exclusive; when a sample matches multiple patterns, we assign the structurally most specific mode (PG $>$ CE $>$ TS).
The non-hacking rate is an upper bound on genuine reasoning, as classifier recall is unknown for most modes.
We report both classifications in \S\ref{sec:experiments}.

Low ISR signals redundancy under exec-only but metric gaming under ISR-as-reward; the mode breakdown, not the ISR scalar, licenses interpretation.

lines: ISR quantifies component redundancy, not semantic faithfulness; its diagnostic value is realized through the downstream mode breakdown (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}), not the scalar alone.
We report \emph{proved-only} ISR (denoted ISR$^*$) throughout to avoid conflating component necessity with prove rate.
-\paragraph{Limitations of ISR.}
-ISR captures component necessity, not semantic faithfulness; it does not correlate with NLI accuracy (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).

-A structural confound arises from component count: formalizations with fewer components mechanically receive higher ISR, and tautological shortcuts ($P{\to}P$) achieve high ISR by construction since the sole premise is necessary for the trivial proof.

-We therefore combine ISR with text-match classifiers for complete hacking detection (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}; $O(1)$ binary variant in Appendix~\ref{app:o1-ablation}), and report premise-count-matched comparisons in \S\ref{sec:goodhart}.
-At the per-sample level, ISR flags distinct failure modes ($\text{ISR}{=}0$: redundancy; $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ with $n{=}1$: tautology) independent of this confound.

-We distinguish two uses of ISR: as an \emph{aggregate} metric (mean ISR across a test set, susceptible to premise-count inflation discussed in \S\ref{sec:goodhart}), and as a \emph{per-sample} diagnostic (the LOO result for a single proof, unaffected by cross-sample length distributions).

-As a diagnostic, ISR most readily identifies CE, where removing fabricated expressions collapses the proof ($\text{ISR}{\approx}0$), but is less discriminative for TS, where tautological structures score high ISR by construction; detecting TS requires combining ISR with component-count thresholds (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}).
\paragraph{LOO independence assumption.}

LOO ablation tests individual, not joint, component necessity~\citep{jia-harman-survey}, systematically underestimating ISR when jointly-necessary components exist; the observed collapse is therefore conservative.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. \section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related-work}

\paragraph{Neurosymbolic reasoning.}
LLM-solver pipelines~\citep{satlm, logic-lm, linc, fover-pei2025, lorp} and RL methods trained on solver feedback~\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl, deepseek-prover-v15, deepseek-r1} evaluate execution accuracy alone, with no diagnostic for component necessity.
AlphaProof~\citep{alphaproof2025} and DeepSeek-Prover-V2~\citep{deepseek-prover-v2} apply RL-based formal verification at scale in Lean~4 for competition mathematics; STA-style diagnostics could probe whether similar structural degeneration occurs in these settings.
We use FOLIO~\citep{folio}, the only public NLI benchmark with both FOL and Prolog annotations.

\paragraph{Reward hacking and Goodhart's Law.}
Goodhart's Law is established theoretically~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy, skalse-reward-hacking, karwowski-goodhart-rl} and empirically in RLHF~\citep{gao-reward-overoptimization} and logical formalization~\citep{bondarenko-spec-gaming, kim-game-formalization}.
Most closely related, \citet{kim-game-formalization} document inference-time gaming on FOLIO with frontier models and Lean~4; our work is complementary in studying training-time degeneration with component necessity rather than faithfulness, and combining STA with inference-time detection would provide full gaming coverage.
\citet{kwa-catastrophic-goodhart} show that heavy-tailed reward misspecification causes catastrophic Goodhart where KL regularization provably fails, a theoretical lens for why GRPO's KL penalty does not prevent our observed collapse.
Reward model ensembles~\citep{coste2023reward} and constrained optimization~\citep{moskovitz2023confronting} address overoptimization at the reward level; STA instead diagnoses structural consequences at the output level.
Concurrent work documents spurious signals in RLVR~\citep{spurious-rewards, yan2026spurious, dong2026probing, metr-reward-hacking} and proposes composite rewards as mitigations~\citep{tarek2025reward, pronesti2026beyond}; \citet{yue2025rl-reasoning} show RLVR redistributes base-model probability mass rather than creating new reasoning, consistent with our finding that GRPO exploits existing shortcuts.
\citet{helff2026gaming} propose Input Perturbation Testing (IPT) for gaming detection; STA shares the perturbation intuition but operates at the component level in neurosymbolic settings where gaming emerges during training.
While IPT perturbs \emph{inputs} to detect inference-time gaming, STA performs leave-one-out ablation on \emph{solver-input components} to diagnose training-time structural degeneration, operating at component-level rather than input-level granularity and targeting the training process rather than deployment behavior.
\citet{khalifa2026countdown} provide controlled testbeds showing that reward hacking in Countdown emerges progressively during training; STA complements such testbeds by offering a component-level diagnostic applicable to neurosymbolic pipelines.
\citet{nishimura2026specgaming} systematically benchmark specification gaming across reasoning models, finding that RL training substantially increases exploit rates; our STA results provide a mechanistic view of how such gaming manifests as structural degeneration in solver traces.
Our Goodhart effect follows the regressional pattern~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} on FOLIO, with extremal dynamics at high $\beta$; its application to a diagnostic designed to \emph{detect} gaming, and the dataset-dependent asymmetry it reveals, are to our knowledge novel.
Complementarily, \citet{wilhelm2026monitoring} detect reward hacking at generation time via internal activations, whereas STA provides a post-training structural diagnostic.

\paragraph{Mutation testing.}
STA adapts the LOO mutation paradigm~\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey} to solver inputs; novelty lies in application and findings, not in the perturbation primitive.

\paragraph{Mutation testing.}
STA adapts the LOO mutation paradigm~\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey} to solver inputs; novelty lies in application and findings, not in the perturbation primitive.

- Originality: 3 — LOO 本身不新，应用场景+Goodhart 发现有贡献

[severity: info] **当前状态合理，有两个小改进空间：**

(a) **conclusion L5 "applicable in principle" 是纯推测。** "math reasoning with formal verifiers, code generation with test suites" 未经任何实验验证。建议加 "pending empirical validation"：
```
STA is applicable in principle to any RL system whose output is verified by a deterministic checker---math reasoning with formal verifiers, code generation with test suites---though empirical validation beyond logic programming remains future work.
```
这防止审稿人质问 "where is the evidence for this generalization?"

(b) **conclusion 缺 practitioner takeaway。** 当前指向 Appendix practical-guidelines 但正文无一句概括。可在 L9 前加一句：
```
For practitioners, the key implication is that structural diagnostics should be used post-hoc rather than as training rewards; the mode breakdown, not the scalar, is the reliable signal.
```

## 2. Limitations 表述

[severity: info] **基本稳固，一个潜在攻击面：**

Limitations L6 "suggesting degeneration is a byproduct of reward optimization success rather than an inherent property of GRPO" — 这个 claim 基于 2/5 non-converging seeds 保留 genuine reasoning。审稿人可能反驳："2 个不收敛的 seed 当然不退化——它们什么都没学到，这不证明退化是 optimization success 的 byproduct，而是 trivially 因为优化压力不足。" 当前 "suggesting" 措辞足够弱，不构成 critical，但如果审稿人追问，rebuttal 要准备："we agree this is correlational, not causal; the non-converging seeds control for the absence of optimization pressure."

EMNLP 要求 limitations 放正文（用户规则已遵守 ✓），"3 个点左右" 指引下当前 6 个点但仅 8 行——简洁度可接受。

## 3. Abstract/Introduction 叙事弧

[severity: warning] **Abstract 缺失 C3。**

当前 abstract 6 行覆盖了 C1（STA/ISR）和 C2（seed-dependent Goodhart），但 C3（cross-logic/cross-benchmark evidence）完全不提。如果 C3 重要到列为独立贡献，abstract 应至少有一个从句。建议在 L6 "persists across logic types and dataset families" 后加半句：
```
...persists across logic types and dataset families---confirmed by cross-logic (Prolog) and cross-benchmark (ProofFOL) replication---: structural proxies...
```
这从 "暗示" 升级为 "明确陈述"，让 C3 在 abstract 中可见。

[severity: info] **C2 在 intro L35 过于冗长。** 当前 C2 是一句 50+ 词的长句（含 3/5 vs 2/5 细节、controls 提及）。Contribution 列表应该 punchy。建议压缩 seed 细节到 §4.3 引用：
```
(\textbf{C2})~empirical characterization of a seed-dependent Goodhart effect when ISR is repurposed as reward, with matched controls ruling out confounds (\S\ref{sec:goodhart});
```
"3/5 vs 2/5" 在 abstract L6 已说过，intro contribution list 不需要重复。

## 4. 全文一致性

[severity: info] **删除后无断裂，无悬空引用。** 逐项确认：

- Related Work：Lanham/Turpin 已移至 mutation testing 段 L24 半句保留 ✓
- Method：ISR limitations 段删除后，L48 保留核心 caveat ✓
- 无 `\ref{}` 指向已删内容 ✓
- "model-agnostic" → 全文 0 匹配 ✓
- "converts" → 全文 0 匹配 ✓
- "reasoning quality" → 全文 0 匹配 ✓

**一个一致性问题：** "observe-vs-optimize asymmetry" 在 abstract L6 和 intro L27 出现，但 conclusion 不使用这个术语——conclusion L4 用 "easier to observe than to optimize" 但未回扣 "asymmetry" 概念。这不是 critical，但回扣会更完整。

**"confirming" 过度使用：** experiments 主文 4 次 + appendix 6 次 = 10 次。"confirming" 暗示 confirmatory analysis，但多数情况是 exploratory。建议将 experiments L28、L37 中的 "confirming" 替换为 "consistent with" 或 "establishing"（L28 的 87% CE 是 primary observation 不是 confirmation；L37 的 SFT comparison 也是）。这是审稿人可能标注的 AI 风格/overclaim 问题。

## 5. 可操作写作改进建议（48h 内可执行，按 ROI 排序）

| # | 改动 | 位置 | ROI | 风险 |
|---|------|------|-----|------|
| W1 | Abstract 加 C3 半句 | abstract L6 | **高** | 低 |
| W2 | 压缩 intro C2 长度 | intro L35 | 中 | 低 |
| W3 | Conclusion 加 practitioner takeaway | conclusion L8-9 | 中 | 低 |
| W4 | Conclusion L5 加 "empirical validation" caveat | conclusion L5 | 中 | 低 |
| W5 | 替换 2-3 处 "confirming" 为更精确动词 | experiments L28, L37 | 中 | 低 |
| W6 | Related Work L15-16 IPT 对比去重 | related_work L15-16 | 低 | 低 |

**不建议做的：**
- 不要改 abstract 开头 hook——当前足够强，改动风险大于收益
- 不要重组 experiments 结构——三轮审稿从未要求
- 不要加更多 hedge——当前 hedging 已在审稿人耐心边界

**诚实回答：纯写作改进不太可能从 3.0 到 3.5。** 三轮 3.0 的核心限制是：
1. 单模型（结构性）
2. N=3-5 seeds 统计功效弱（结构性）
3. 无 mitigation/solution（conceptual）
4. LOO 方法本身 novelty 有限（conceptual）

W1-W5 可以消除一些 minor deductions，但不会改变评分区间。最乐观估计：W1-W5 全部执行后 3.0-3.25，Excitement 可能恢复 3.0。建议执行 W1-W4（4 处微调，30 分钟工作量），把时间花在 rebuttal 准备上。

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	We evaluate STA along three axes: ISR as a diagnostic for reward hacking (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}); ISR as a training reward, where it exhibits Goodhart effects (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}); and cross-domain generalization across logic types and dataset families (\S\ref{sec:crossdomain}).
5	A hacking taxonomy synthesizes the modes observed across conditions (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
6	
7	\subsection{Setup}\label{sec:setup}
8	
9	We train Qwen3-4B~\citep{qwen3} with GRPO~\citep{deepseekmath} ($K{=}4$, lr $10^{-6}$, 500 steps default, 1000 where noted) over seeds $\{42,43,44\}$ (ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ extends to $\{45,46\}$; Appendix~\ref{app:detailed-results}) on a fixed 500-example FOLIO~\citep{folio} subset held constant across all conditions; the SFT baseline uses negative log-likelihood on gold formalizations.\footnote{Seeds control initialization and rollout sampling; all conditions share the same fixed training subset.}
10	Held-out evaluation uses 100 FOLIO examples with greedy decoding;\footnote{Seed~43 uses nucleus sampling ($T{=}0.7$) due to greedy-mode degeneration; excluding s43 yields consistent or stronger collapse: at 1000 steps, both remaining seeds show ${\leq}7\%$ non-hacking (Appendix~\ref{app:detailed-results}).} all cross-run ISR values are recomputed uniformly by a single evaluator so training-log ISR is never compared across runs.
11	Cross-dataset experiments (\S\ref{sec:crossdomain}) use ProofFOL, a silver-standard FOL corpus of ${\sim}$500 training examples constructed by translating ProofWriter~\citep{proofwriter} problems via GPT-4o and filtering through Prover9 (${\sim}70\%$ retention); \emph{stable convergence} denotes $\overline{\text{PR}}_{\text{final\,50}} > 0.90$.
12	We report prove rate (PR), proved-only ISR ($\text{ISR}^*$), hacking-mode rates from a two-stage classifier (strict text matching for CE/TS plus functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\text{necessary}}$ distribution; \S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}), and a \emph{non-hacking} (N-H) rate, an upper bound on genuine reasoning: the residual matching none of the eight cataloged patterns (classifier recall unknown; 152-sample precision audit in Appendix~\ref{app:hacking-modes}).
13	
14	\paragraph{Statistical considerations.}
15	With three seeds exhibiting multi-attractor dynamics, per-seed qualitative analysis is the primary framework; the divergence itself is a finding.
16	Pooled statistics (CMH) serve as supplementary reference; CMH treats within-seed samples as independent observations from a single trained model, so the true replication count is $N{=}3$ seeds.
17	At $N{=}3$, seed-level tests achieve 80\% power only for very large effects ($d{\geq}3.0$); non-significant comparisons (e.g., prevalence $p{=}0.182$) are exploratory.
18	CMH $p$-values are reported as descriptive summaries of the stratified association; with $N{=}3$ strata they should not be interpreted as formal inference over the seed population.
19	An $N{=}2$ sensitivity analysis excluding s43 confirms consistent or stronger patterns: both remaining seeds reach ${\leq}7\%$ non-hacking at 500 steps (Appendix~\ref{app:n2-sensitivity}).
20	ProofFOL results ($p{=}0.10$, $N{=}3$) are exploratory and underpowered.
21	
22	\subsection{ISR as Diagnostic}
23	\label{sec:diagnostic}
24	
25	\textbf{Collapse trajectory.}
26	Figure~\ref{fig:training-isr-curves} traces exec-only GRPO (seed~42) across 1000 training steps.
27	As PR climbs from $32\%$ to $96\%$, ISR$^*$ collapses from $0.642$ to $0.003$, a $214\times$ raw drop (partially attributable to premise-count inflation; matched comparison yields $1.06\times$, \S\ref{sec:goodhart}) consistent with structural degeneration behind apparent success. %% registry: plan003-eval-exec-only-r5, plan001-exec-only-s42-r2, plan016-extended-1000-s42
28	By 500 steps, $87\%$ of proved samples embed the conclusion verbatim (CE), confirming degeneration independent of the ISR scalar.
29	A binary variant testing only collective premise necessity misses the collapse entirely ($\text{ISR}{=}1.0$ for all proved samples), confirming that per-component LOO testing is essential (Appendix~\ref{app:o1-ablation}).
30	
31	\textbf{Cross-seed instability.}
32	Three seeds diverge into qualitatively different failure modes: conclusion embedding (s42), repetition collapse (s43), and tautological collapse (s44), yet all converge to ${\leq}7\%$ non-hacking by 1000 steps (Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}; Appendix~\ref{app:detailed-results}).
33	Exec-only seeds exhibit qualitatively different convergence patterns (PR range: 13--98\%), precluding meaningful pooling; we report seed~42 as representative of the converged regime (Table~\ref{tab:goodhart-landscape}). %% registry: plan001-exec-only-s42-r2, plan001-exec-only-s43-r4, plan001-exec-only-s44; plan016-extended-1000-s42, plan001-exec-only-s43-1000-r7, plan001-exec-only-s44-1000-r2
34	Two additional seeds under identical conditions fail to converge ($\text{PR}{\approx}14\%$; Appendix~\ref{app:seed-convergence}), retaining genuine reasoning and suggesting that structural degeneration requires successful RL optimization as a prerequisite (Appendix~\ref{app:llama-coldstart}).
35	
36	\textbf{SFT baseline.}
37	SFT on gold formalizations produces $92\%$ non-hacking outputs at $\text{PR}{=}13\%$ ($\text{OR}{=}147$ vs.\ exec-only, $p{<}0.001$), confirming that hacking modes are absent before RL optimization.
38	SFT serves as a pre-RL reference rather than a PR-matched control; its low PR reflects minimal optimization pressure.
39	Early-training comparison supports this interpretation: at 100 steps ($\text{PR}{=}32\%$), hacking already reaches $31\%$ vs.\ SFT's $8\%$ at comparable PR (Appendix~\ref{app:100step}). %% registry: plan009-sft-baseline-s42-1000/s43-1000/s44-1000-r3
40	
41	\subsection{Goodhart Effects on ISR-as-Reward}
42	\label{sec:goodhart}
43	
44	We reverse ISR's role from observer to reward: $r = r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1 + \beta\,\text{ISR})$, with matched random control ($u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$).
45	The result is a regressional Goodhart pattern~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy}: optimizing a structural proxy shifts the \emph{composition} of failure modes without reducing their aggregate prevalence.
46	ISR reward systematically selects for tautological shortcuts (TS) over conclusion embedding (CE) rather than producing genuine reasoning (Table~\ref{tab:goodhart-landscape}). The scalar ISR$^*$ advantage ($214\times$ raw) collapses to $1.06\times$ after controlling for premise count; the compositional mode shift provides the primary evidence.
47	
48	\paragraph{Multiplicative coupling.}
49	The multiplicative reward formulation conflates ISR signal with interaction effects; three controls constrain this confound: exec-only's convergence to pure hacking, the qualitative TS shift under ISR, and an additive variant that did not converge (Appendix~\ref{app:setup}); the shuffled-ISR control partially addresses the coupling by preserving ISR's distribution while breaking sample-level semantics.
50	The shuffled-ISR control produces SFT-like outcomes ($87\%$ non-hacking at low PR), consistent with the Goodhart effect requiring the sample-level ISR signal, not its distributional shape (corroborating rather than definitive given $N{=}46$ proved samples).

Per-seed data in Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}. $^\ddagger$ISR$^*$ raw mean inflated by TS gaming; $1.06\times$ is the premise-count-matched value relative to random (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}, Appendix~\ref{app:detailed-results}); 5-seed raw ISR$^*$ in parentheses (same confound, no matched control). $^\P$Includes TS classifier false-negative correction (s44) and PG premise-subset gaming (s42; 5.2\% of proved; Appendix~\ref{app:h8}). $^\S$Random TS driven entirely by seed~43 (38.3\%); seeds~42/44: 0\%. Per-seed breakdown: Appendix Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}. Shuffled-ISR is a deconfounding control (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}), not an independent condition. ISR$^*$ reported for completeness; mode-level analysis (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}) provides the primary diagnostic.}

76	\textbf{Low-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.1$).}
77	ISR reward amplifies TS convergence: $71\%$ of proved samples under ISR exhibit tautological shortcuts vs.\ $14\%$ under random (Appendix~\ref{app:statistical-details}). %% registry: plan002 vs plan018 all seeds; D095 FINAL
78	TS is the canonical Goodhart move: a single premise identical to the conclusion yields $\text{ISR}\geq 0.5$ by construction, directly satisfying the LOO metric (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}).
79	Total conclusion embedding ($\text{CE}+\text{TS}$) spans $68$--$100\%$ across both conditions; the composition shifts (CE dominates under random, TS under ISR) without reducing aggregate hacking (Figure~\ref{fig:hacking-composition}).
80	A seed-stratified $\chi^2$ test confirms the overall mode distribution differs significantly between ISR and random conditions ($\chi^2{=}174.8$, $\text{df}{=}2$, $p{<}10^{-38}$; Appendix~\ref{app:statistical-details}).
81	
82	\textbf{Seed-dependent outcomes.}
83	ISR reward produces bimodal outcomes: 3/5 seeds converge to gaming ($\text{N-H}{\leq}6\%$), while 2/5 retain substantial genuine reasoning (${\sim}55\%$), demonstrating that the Goodhart effect is seed-dependent rather than universal (seeds~45/46 added post-hoc to test replication; Appendix~\ref{app:detailed-results}).
84	
85	\textbf{Premise-count confound.}
86	The $214\times$ raw ISR$^*$ collapse is largely explained by premise-count reduction: ISR-trained models produce shorter formalizations that mechanically inflate ISR.
87	The premise-count-matched comparison yields only $1.06\times$ (McNemar $p{=}0.317$, $n{=}100$ matched pairs; Appendix~\ref{app:premise-count}), indicating that the scalar ISR advantage is not statistically significant.
88	
89	The compositional evidence, however, survives this control.
90	In the modal premise-count range (4--6 premises, where most proved samples fall), TS reaches $19.7\%$ under ISR versus $0\%$ under random reward (Table~\ref{tab:premise-bin-modes}).
91	TS hacking is mechanistically limited to simpler problems---models cannot restate the conclusion while ignoring all premises when formalization complexity is high.
92	This complexity dependence is a mechanistic insight, not a confound: the compositional mode shift---not the scalar ISR difference---constitutes the primary evidence for the Goodhart effect.
93	The failure of ISR-as-reward demonstrates that structural diagnostics cannot be naively repurposed as training objectives---a finding that applies to any LOO-based metric in solver-verified settings.
94	
95	\textbf{Higher doses and temporal dynamics.}
96	Any genuine reasoning under ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ is transient: non-hacking drops from $17\%$ to $2\%$ by 1000 steps as TS escalates (Figure~\ref{fig:training-isr-curves}). %% registry: plan002-b01-s42-1000, plan016-extended-1000-s42

1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	STA exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation; repurposed as reward, ISR produces a seed-dependent Goodhart effect, documenting that structural proxies for formalization integrity are easier to observe than to optimize (Appendix~\ref{app:practical-guidelines}).
5	STA is applicable in principle to any RL system whose output is verified by a deterministic checker---math reasoning with formal verifiers, code generation with test suites---wherever solver-verifiable structure can be ablated.
6	Cross-logic (Prolog) and cross-benchmark (ProofFOL) experiments confirm that the compositional mode shift generalizes beyond FOL-FOLIO, though the dominant hacking mode varies by dataset (\S\ref{sec:crossdomain}).
7	Our cross-scale results hint at a capacity-dependent pattern: structural degeneration may require model capacity sufficient for RL convergence but insufficient to resist structural shortcuts. The high non-convergence rate among exec-only seeds (two of five fail to converge; Appendix~\ref{app:seed-convergence}) further suggests degeneration requires successful convergence as a prerequisite.
8	As an aggregate metric, ISR is susceptible to premise-count confounds (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}); per-sample mode classification offers a more reliable diagnostic pathway for future work.
9	Combining STA with inference-time gaming detection~\citep{kim-game-formalization, helff2026gaming} could extend structural monitoring across the training--deployment spectrum.

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

STA exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation; repurposed as reward, ISR produces a seed-dependent Goodhart effect, documenting that structural proxies for formalization integrity are easier to observe than to optimize (Appendix~\ref{app:practical-guidelines}).
STA is applicable in principle to any RL system whose output is verified by a deterministic checker---math reasoning with formal verifiers, code generation with test suites---wherever solver-verifiable structure can be ablated.
Cross-logic (Prolog) and cross-benchmark (ProofFOL) experiments confirm that the compositional mode shift generalizes beyond FOL-FOLIO, though the dominant hacking mode varies by dataset (\S\ref{sec:crossdomain}).
Our cross-scale results hint at a capacity-dependent pattern: structural degeneration may require model capacity sufficient for RL convergence but insufficient to resist structural shortcuts. The high non-convergence rate among exec-only seeds (two of five fail to converge; Appendix~\ref{app:seed-convergence}) further suggests degeneration requires successful convergence as a prerequisite.
As an aggregate metric, ISR is susceptible to premise-count confounds (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}); per-sample mode classification offers a more reliable diagnostic pathway for future work.
Combining STA with inference-time gaming detection~\citep{kim-game-formalization, helff2026gaming} could extend structural monitoring across the training--deployment spectrum.
